brief.headline: Offer 15-day faster payment in exchange for a ~12% price cut — their 12.16% borrowing cost makes early cash worth that much to them.

priceAsk.summary: Target a discount of approximately 12% in exchange for accelerated payment
priceAsk.target: Benchmark raw BOPET film substrate at 171.60 ₹/kg (import unit value) and negotiate conversion charges separately; demand a price concession tied to our 12.16% early-payment value
priceAsk.basis: Their effective borrowing cost is 12.16%, so paying us 15 days faster saves them that rate on the freed working capital. Additionally, their 101d cash-conversion cycle is well above the 64d peer median, meaning cash velocity is expensive for them. We can trade payment speed for price.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Offer to move from 30 Days After Receipt to 15 Days After Receipt in exchange for a price cut
paymentTermAsk.cashImpact: Accelerating by 15 days would free ₹26.60 L of our working capital; for them it compresses their 101d cash cycle and is worth their 12.16% borrowing rate

brief.financialLeverage: Shrinath's 2.3% net margin sits just below the 2.5% peer median, and their 1.25x debt-to-equity ratio plus 1.94x interest coverage show they are levered and servicing debt actively. The Altman Z-score of 2.36 puts them in the grey zone — not distressed, but not robust. Their 12.16% effective borrowing cost and 101d cash-conversion cycle (vs 64d peer median) mean early payment is valuable to them. We represent only 0.61% of their ₹1064.86 Cr revenue, so we are not a make-or-break customer. However, the CARE BBB+ / Stable rating and EPF payment delays are yellow flags. Push firmly on payment-for-price, but avoid a squeeze that tips a grey-zone supplier into trouble.

evidence.point: Their borrowing cost is high, making early cash worth a double-digit discount to them
Their cash is tied up far longer than peers, so they value payment speed
They already stretch their own suppliers well past the peer norm
Their balance sheet carries meaningful debt
Margins are thin, leaving little room for deep price cuts without risk to supply
We are a small customer, limiting our individual negotiating weight

alternates.name: Huhtamaki India Ltd
alternates.why: Listed flexible-packaging converter already supplying FDC in small volumes — proven, scalable second source for laminate sachets with ₹2611.64 Cr revenue and B (64/100) health score

alternates.name: UFLEX Ltd
alternates.why: Listed flexibles giant covering both film substrate and conversion at ₹16492.00 Cr revenue — can second-source laminates at scale with integrated supply chain

alternates.name: Constantia Parikh Packaging Pvt Ltd
alternates.why: Global Constantia group's India converter specialising in pharma blister and sachet laminates — strong technical fit for GEEP sachets at ₹222.04 Cr revenue

risks: Altman Z-score of 2.36 puts them in the grey zone — push too hard and we risk tipping a fragile supplier into distress, threatening our own supply continuity
EPF payment delays and CARE BBB+ / Stable rating are yellow flags — qualify alternates now in case financial stress escalates
Their 2.3% net margin leaves almost no cushion for deep price cuts — frame the ask as payment-for-price swap, not a margin squeeze
We are only 0.61% of their revenue, so we lack the volume clout to dictate terms unilaterally — lead with the mutual win of faster cash against lower price
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We'd like to help you improve your cash cycle — if we move to 15-day payment, we expect a price reduction in line with the 12.16% borrowing cost you'll save on that early cash.
